title: Pharming pauses Ruconest production over fill-finish issue, threatening US supply
snippet: A problem at a third-party manufacturer prompted Pharming to pause production of its cornerstone drug and warn that supply constraints are likely.

title: Capricor could lay off hundreds in wake of FDA rejection
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: ‘Buckle up’: Opdivo biosimilar settlement sets BMS up for make-or-break moment
snippet: Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb have reached a settlement over PD-1 drug Opdivo, allowing biosimilar entry to the market in 2028.

title: Alkem draws FDA warning letter over dissolution, complaint-handling lapses
snippet: Visiting months after a recall of tablets made at the Indian plant, FDA inspectors identified problems with Alkem’s investigations of unexpected dissolution test results, among other issues.

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Sanofi’s $41B Insmed buy, Capricor’s second rejection, FDA’s pre-holiday rush
snippet: Sanofi inked the biggest biopharma buyout since Pfizer’s $43 billion acquisition of Seagen in 2023; Capricor’s cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy was denied again by the FDA, which cited data intergrity issues in a rare statement; but several other companies have fared better at the regulator, including Rege...

title: Sanofi’s $41B megadeal lands as pharma enjoys macro boost in turbid markets
snippet: The largest pharma deal since Pfizer’s 2023 Seagen acquisition has helped buoy M&A sentiment in the sector, which has become a safe haven for investors as the markets reel from the NVIDIA drama.

title: 5 biotechs poised to take the IPO plunge
snippet: PitchBook has picked a handful of biotechs likely to go public soon—potentially even joining the already 2026’s bumper class—based on dealmaking activity, history and financial maturity.

title: Summit’s ivonescimab optimism meets FDA scrutiny
snippet: A look at how Summit Therapeutics framed ivonescimab’s clinical results compared with how the FDA weighed the evidence behind its application

title: Roche’s Genentech notches 2nd breast cancer approval for oral SERD in a week
snippet: The FDA approval of Wilserdly—the first new hormone therapy option for patients with early-stage breast cancer in more than 20 years—is the second straight greenlight for Roche’s drug, which got the nod for an advanced breast cancer subtype last week.

title: ProMIS’ new CCO is ready to write next chapter in Alzheimer’s after leaving Biogen
snippet: Ivana Rubino has joined neurodegenerative biotech ProMIS Neurosciences as chief commercial officer, with 15 years of experience in the brutal Alzheimer’s field as her guide.

title: BMS loses CFO to Coca-Cola on heels of R&D overhaul
snippet: The announcement comes less than two weeks after Bristol Myers Squibb merged its research and development departments under one leader.

title: Sanofi’s new CEO Garijo strikes 2026’s largest pharma deal with $41B for Insmed
snippet: Insmed will bolster Sanofi’s immunology and inflammation portfolio, which is currently led by Regeneron-partnered blockbuster Dupixent.

title: Biotech’s fear of global expansion is overblown, risks destroying asset value
snippet: The perceived threat of Most Favored Nation drug pricing is keeping many companies out of international markets. But for some medicines, the costs of delaying entry run high.

title: FDA approves BridgeBio’s Welgemda as 1st targeted therapy for rare muscle disease
snippet: Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas called the approval of BridgeBio’s limb-girdle muscular dystrophy therapy “a historic milestone” for patients and families living with the disease.

title: Erasca’s early data show profile that could challenge RevMed in pancreatic cancer: Analysts
snippet: In updated Phase 1 data, Erasca’s ERAS-0015 showed a robust response rate in pancreatic cancer subgroups where Revolution Medicines’ recently-approved Rasonque was weaker, leading Jefferies to write that the investigational molecular glue could have an advantage over the approved therapy.

title: Sharon Mates’ next act: Ritzey banks $112M to target Down syndrome and diabetes
snippet: After J&J’s $14.6 billion buyout of Intra-Cellular Therapies, the biotech’s former CEO Sharon Mates is still chasing intracellular signaling, this time with Ritzey Therapeutics for metabolic and neurologic diseases.

title: Invivyd plans FDA run for COVID-19 preventative, teeing up ‘new era for immunization’
snippet: Invivyd plans on ushering in a “new era for immunization” with its COVID-19 prevention antibody that is designed using the same antibody backbone as the biotech’s emergency-authorized Pemgarda.

title: Lilly’s 15th M&A deal of 2026 brings LoQus23’s Huntington’s work in house for $725M
snippet: LoQus23 Therapeutics is a good match for Eli Lilly’s professed goal of finding biotechs that provide small, early, risky bets.

title: Capricor CEO says FDA never gave DMD cell therapy a ‘fair shake’
snippet: The FDA rejected Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy for a second time on Friday, citing data integrity issues. CEO Linda Marbán told BioSpace she was shocked and explains why she thinks this reason is suspect.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
